title: By the winds that scatter far and wide.
subtitle: The first witness in a chain of oaths
then: Ali bin Abi Talib stood on the pulpit in Kufah and invited questions on any verse. A man asked about adh-dhariyat. {idea}The wind,{/idea} Ali said. Ibn Kathir explains these oaths climb in order, from lower to higher, and together they are {idea}a vow from Allah that the Resurrection will come.{/idea}
now: Wind rattles the window, or scatters leaves across the car park as you hurry to work. You cannot see it, only what it moves. {idea}Allah swears by it.{/idea} The unseen is not unreal.
old: Wind is just air moving, nothing more.
new: The wind is a sign Allah swears by, unseen yet moving everything, pointing to His promise.
try: Next time you feel the wind today, pause and say SubhanAllah once.

title: And by the clouds carrying their heavy load.
subtitle: Tons of water floating above you
then: Ali said the laden ones are {idea}the clouds.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes the winds bring the clouds, which is why they come next in the oath. Each sworn thing rises a step higher, building toward one claim: {idea}what you are promised is true.{/idea}
now: A grey sky before a storm, and you groan about your laundry on the line. {reward}Above you hangs a weight of water carried gently until it is needed.{/reward} Allah swears by that load.
old: Clouds just mean bad weather is coming.
new: The clouds carry a heavy gift by Allah's command, and He swears by them.
try: Look up at the clouds once today and think of them as carrying provision for someone.

title: And by the ships that sail along with ease.
subtitle: Gliding forward, held by a power not their own
then: Ali explained al-jariyat as {idea}the ships.{/idea} Some scholars said it refers to the stars that float in their orbits with ease, which fits the rising order: winds, then clouds, then stars, then angels. Either way, {idea}they move with an ease they did not make.{/idea}
now: A container ship on the horizon, a plane at night that looks like a moving star. You take it for granted that heavy things glide. {idea}Ease is given.{/idea} The same is true of the easy days in your own life.
old: When things go smoothly, it is because I planned well.
new: Ease in motion, for ships, stars, or my day, is something Allah grants.
try: When something goes smoothly today, say Alhamdulillah before taking credit.

title: And by the angels who distribute each matter.
subtitle: The top of the ladder of oaths
then: Ali said the distributors of command are {idea}the angels.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains they are above the stars and {idea}descend with Allah's orders and the decrees He determines.{/idea} The chain of oaths has reached its top, and the claim is about to come.
now: Bonus season, and you are anxious about what share you will get. The spreadsheet decides, you think. {idea}Above every spreadsheet, the angels carry out what Allah apportions.{/idea} That does not stop you working; it stops the panic.
old: My share in life is decided by the people above me.
new: Every share is apportioned by Allah's command, carried out by His angels.
try: Before checking your pay or results this week, say: O Allah, bless what You have apportioned for me.

title: What you are promised is true.
subtitle: The point of all four oaths
then: After swearing by winds, clouds, ships and angels, Allah states the point: {reward}what you are promised is surely true.{/reward} Ibn Kathir calls it a truthful promise. The surah was revealed while the Prophet's ﷺ message was met with {trap}denial and ridicule.{/trap}
now: A landlord who never fixed the boiler. A friend who said he would call. A company that promised a refund. {trap}You learn to expect broken promises.{/trap} {reward}This one is sworn by the whole sky.{/reward}
old: Every promise comes with a chance it will not happen.
new: Allah's promise is the one promise that is never broken.
try: Keep one small promise you made to someone this week, today.

title: And the Recompense will surely happen.
subtitle: Every deed comes back to its owner
then: The oaths confirm a second fact: {idea}ad-din, the Recompense, will surely come to pass.{/idea} Maududi notes the surah mostly deals with the Hereafter, against people who built their views on guesswork about what follows death.
now: You helped a neighbor move and no one thanked you. You held your tongue in a family fight and nobody noticed. {reward}None of it vanishes.{/reward} {idea}The Recompense means every quiet effort is counted.{/idea}
old: If no one sees or rewards it, it was wasted.
new: Every deed, seen or unseen, will meet its recompense.
try: Do one kind thing today that you know no one will thank you for.

title: By the sky full of beautiful pathways.
subtitle: A woven, perfect heaven as witness
then: A new oath: by the sky of hubuk. Ibn Abbas said {idea}full of beauty, grace, magnificence and perfection.{/idea} Ad-Dahhak compared it to the ripples wind carves in water, sand and plants. Ibn Kathir says all the meanings return to {idea}beauty and intricate structure.{/idea}
now: You see a photo of the night sky from a dark desert, the Milky Way like a woven path. Then you look up from your city street and see orange haze. {idea}The pattern is still there.{/idea} Allah swears by it to make a point about you.
old: The sky is beautiful, but it has nothing to say to me.
new: A sky this ordered is sworn by to show how disordered my guesses can be.
try: Find a photo or a real view of the night sky today and look at it for a full minute.

title: You are lost in conflicting words.
subtitle: A perfect sky above, confused opinions below
then: Sworn by the ordered sky: {trap}you are in conflicting speech.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says their opinions did not connect or agree. Qatadah said some admitted the Quran was true while others denied it. Maududi notes such clashing beliefs about the end show {trap}they were built on guesswork, not knowledge.{/trap}
now: A podcast says there is nothing after death. A video says you come back as someone else. A friend says just be a good person and it will be fine. {trap}All confident, all clashing.{/trap} {idea}Clashing guesses are a sign that none of them is knowledge.{/idea}
old: There are so many views about death that no one can really know.
new: The confusion of opinions is exactly why I need knowledge from the One who made the sky.
try: Next time you hear a strong claim about the afterlife, ask: is this from knowledge or a guess?

title: Only the one already turning away is turned away.
subtitle: Who confusion actually fools
then: Ibn Kathir explains that these confused opinions {trap}only fool those who are inwardly misguided.{/trap} Falsehood takes hold in a person already looking for it. Ibn Abbas and As-Suddi said: he who is misguided is led away from it, the Quran.
now: You see a clip mocking religion and it lands harder than usual. Ask honestly: was I already wanting an excuse? {idea}Arguments rarely pull us; they find where we were already leaning.{/idea}
old: I drifted because the doubts were too convincing.
new: Doubts grip the heart that was already turning, so I guard my heart's direction first.
try: Notice one thing that weakens your faith, and ask Allah in a short dua to keep your heart steady.

title: Ruined are those who live by guesses.
subtitle: The guessers about what comes after death
then: Mujahid said the kharrasun are {trap}the liars who claim they will never be brought back.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said: cursed be the doubters. Qatadah said: people of doubt and suspicion. Maududi warns that building your view of the end on {trap}speculation{/trap} wastes a whole life.
now: You would never pick a surgeon by guessing, or sign a mortgage on a hunch. {trap}Yet many people decide what happens after death on a feeling.{/trap} {idea}The biggest question deserves your most careful thinking.{/idea}
old: What happens after death is just a matter of opinion.
new: Guessing about the most important question is the real ruin, so I seek knowledge.
try: Spend fifteen minutes this week reading a passage of the Quran about the Hereafter, slowly.

title: Drowning in a flood, and still playing.
subtitle: Heedless while the water rises
then: The guessers are {trap}within a flood, heedless.{/trap} Ibn Abbas and others said: in disbelief and doubt, they are heedless and playful. The picture is of people up to their necks in something, and too distracted to notice.
now: A weekend that disappears into a series. A month that goes by in notifications and plans. {trap}Fun is not the problem; not noticing the flood is.{/trap} {idea}Lift your head once a day and check the water level.{/idea}
old: I am not doing anything wrong, just having fun.
new: Fun is fine, but heedlessness while the big questions wait is a flood I can drown in.
try: Set one daily reminder on your phone that just says: what am I preparing for?

title: They ask: so when is this Day of Judgment?
subtitle: A question asked to mock, not to learn
then: Ibn Kathir says they asked this {trap}in denial, stubbornness, doubt and suspicion.{/trap} It was not a real question. It was a way of saying it is never coming. The next verse answers them.
now: Someone in a comment thread asks, with a laughing emoji, when the end of the world is supposed to arrive. Maybe a part of you has wondered too. {idea}The date is not yours to know. Your readiness is.{/idea}
old: If I knew when, I would get ready in time.
new: The question that matters is not when, but whether I am ready now.
try: Write down one thing you would fix if you knew the Day was close. Start on it.

title: The answer: the Day they are tried over the Fire.
subtitle: The reply to a mocking question
then: Allah answers their mocking question directly. {trap}It is the Day they will be tried over the Fire.{/trap} Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Al-Hasan said yuftanun means punished. Mujahid compared it to {trap}gold tested in fire.{/trap}
now: Gold is tested in fire to show what it really is. Your days test you in smaller ways: a hard boss, a sick parent, a moment of temptation. {idea}Let the small tests here refine you,{/idea} so the great test does not catch you unprepared.
old: Hard moments are just bad luck to get through.
new: Every trial now is a chance to be refined, so I meet the final trial ready.
try: Face one small test today, a temptation or a difficult task, with patience instead of avoidance.

title: This is what you asked to be hurried.
subtitle: Mocking a warning does not delay it
then: It will be said to them: {trap}taste your trial; this is what you were impatient for.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says these words are spoken to rebuke them, because in the world they dared the Day to come quickly.
now: A doctor warns you about your blood pressure and you joke, we all die of something. A friend warns you about a habit and you laugh it off. {idea}Daring a warning feels brave.{/idea} {reward}The time before it arrives is the gift.{/reward}
old: If the warning were true, it would have happened by now.
new: The delay is not proof it will not come; it is time given to me to change.
try: Take one warning you have joked about, from a doctor, a friend, or a verse, and act on it today.

title: The mindful will be among gardens and springs.
subtitle: The other side of the same Day
then: Right after the scene of the deniers, the surah turns. Ibn Kathir says {reward}those with taqwa will be amid gardens and springs on the Day of their return,{/reward} while the miserable face punishment. The next verses describe who these people were in this life.
now: After a long, hard week of trying to do right, of saying no, waking for Fajr, holding your temper, it can feel like nothing changes. {reward}Gardens and springs are where that road leads.{/reward}
old: Being careful about Allah just makes life harder.
new: Mindfulness of Allah leads to gardens and springs, so the effort is going somewhere.
try: Drink a glass of water slowly today and ask Allah for the springs of Paradise.

title: Taking what their Lord gives, because they did good before.
subtitle: Today's effort, tomorrow's gift
then: Ibn Kathir says the mindful will {reward}receive what their Lord gives them: delight, happiness and favors.{/reward} Why? Because {idea}before that, in the life of the world, they were doers of good.{/idea} He links it to 69:24: eat and drink for what you sent ahead.
now: Every Sunday you visit your grandmother in the care home, though the drive is long and she sometimes forgets your name. {idea}That is before that.{/idea} {reward}The receiving comes later, and it is generous.{/reward}
old: Paradise is something that just happens to good people at the end.
new: What I receive there is what I sent ahead from here, by doing good now.
try: Send one deed ahead today: visit, call, or give to someone who needs it.

title: They slept only a little of the night.
subtitle: A part of every night kept for Allah
then: Ibn Abbas said {idea}every night they would worship Allah, even for a little part.{/idea} Anas said they prayed between Maghrib and Isha. In Madinah the Prophet's ﷺ first words were: feed people, keep family ties, spread salam, {reward}pray at night while people sleep, and enter Paradise in peace.{/reward}
now: Your alarm is set for work, not for prayer. Night prayer feels like something for the very pious. {idea}The scholars said even a small part counts:{/idea} two rak'ahs before bed, or between Maghrib and Isha.
old: Night prayer is for people with much more faith than me.
new: Keeping even a little of the night for Allah is part of being among the doers of good.
try: Pray two extra rak'ahs tonight before you sleep.

title: Before dawn, they were asking forgiveness.
subtitle: The quiet hour when the door is open

picture.label: The last third of the night

then: Mujahid said they were praying. Others said they stood in prayer, then {idea}saved their asking for forgiveness for the hours before dawn.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said Allah descends to the lowest heaven in the last third of the night and asks: {reward}is there anyone seeking forgiveness, that I may forgive him?{/reward}
now: You wake at 4am for no reason, scroll for a bit, and fall back asleep. {reward}That hour is when the question is being asked.{/reward} {idea}Even one astaghfirullah, said with meaning, answers it.{/idea}
old: Forgiveness is for after big sins, not part of my daily rhythm.
new: The hour before dawn is a standing invitation, and asking pardon is how the doers of good end their night.
try: Set an alarm ten minutes before Fajr tomorrow and spend them saying astaghfirullah.

title: In their wealth was a right for the asker and the deprived.
subtitle: Including the needy who never ask
then: After their prayer, their giving. Ibn Kathir says {idea}a designated part{/idea} of their wealth belonged to the asker and the deprived. Aisha said the mahrum is one without a trade to earn from. The Prophet ﷺ said the truly poor is {reward}the one whose need is not known, so no one gives to him.{/reward}
now: The man at the traffic light is easy to see. The colleague quietly skipping lunch to save money, or the single mother at school pick-up who never mentions bills, is not. {idea}The verse asks you to notice the ones who do not ask.{/idea}
old: I give when someone asks me.
new: Part of my wealth is already owed, including to those too proud or quiet to ask.
try: Think of one person who might be struggling quietly, and help them discreetly this week.

title: The earth is full of signs for the certain.
subtitle: Valleys, rivers, people, all pointing one way
then: Ibn Kathir lists the signs: {idea}plants, animals, valleys, mountains, deserts, rivers and oceans,{/idea} and people with different languages, colors, intentions and abilities. They testify to the Creator's power. Maududi notes the surah invites people to study the earth and heavens and test the message against them.
now: On a train, look around the carriage: a dozen languages, faces, stories. Outside the window, fields, a river, a hill. {idea}The whole scene is a page of signs.{/idea} Certainty grows by reading it.
old: I would believe more firmly if I saw something extraordinary.
new: The ordinary earth is already full of signs; certainty is learning to read them.
try: On your next journey, look out the window instead of at your phone and name three signs you see.

title: And in yourselves. Will you not see?
subtitle: The closest sign is your own body
then: After the signs on earth, Allah points inward. Ibn Kathir says He {idea}put every organ in its rightful place.{/idea} Qatadah said whoever thinks about his own creation will see {idea}he was made with flexible joints so that worship is easy for him.{/idea}
now: You bend into sujood without thinking: knees, hands, forehead, all moving together. You blink, breathe, heal a paper cut by tomorrow. {idea}A sign you carry everywhere.{/idea}
old: My body is just something I live in.
new: My own body is a sign of Allah, built so that worship comes easily.
try: In your next sujood, notice for a moment how every joint made that position possible, and thank Him.

title: Your provision is in the sky, and what you are promised.
subtitle: Rain above, Paradise beyond

row.title: in my job
sub: if I lose it, I am lost

then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said {reward}provision in the heaven is the rain,{/reward} and {reward}what you are promised is Paradise.{/reward} Both come from above. The verses about signs end by turning your eyes upward.
now: A redundancy email lands on a Tuesday morning. Your stomach drops because the job felt like where your food came from. {reward}Your provision was always in the heaven.{/reward} {idea}The job was one door it came through.{/idea}
old: My income depends entirely on my employer.
new: My provision is decreed above; jobs are only the doors it comes through.
try: Before you look at your bank balance next, say: O Allah, You are my provider.

title: As true as the fact that you can speak.
subtitle: An oath by the Lord of heaven and earth
then: Allah swears by Himself: {idea}all they were promised, Judgment, Resurrection and Recompense, will certainly occur.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says do not doubt it, just as you do not doubt that you can speak. Mu'adh used to tell his friends: {reward}what I say is as true as your being here.{/reward}
now: Say something out loud right now. You heard it; you do not doubt it happened. {idea}That is the level of certainty this verse asks you to hold about the Day.{/idea}
old: I believe in the Hereafter, but it feels less real than my daily life.
new: The Hereafter is as real as my own voice, sworn by the Lord of heaven and earth.
try: Say out loud today: the meeting with Allah is true. Hear yourself say it.

title: Has the story of Ibrahim's honored guests reached you?
subtitle: A new story begins at a doorstep
then: Allah turns to a story told also in Surah Hud and Al-Hijr. Ibn Kathir says these were {idea}the guests whom Ibrahim honored.{/idea} They were three angels, Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, who came looking like men. {reward}He honored them without knowing who they were.{/reward}
now: A new neighbor knocks to ask for a ladder. A stranger shows up at the masjid after Jumu'ah, alone. {idea}You do not know who they are.{/idea} {reward}Ibrahim did not know either, and he honored them.{/reward}
old: I make an effort for guests who matter.
new: Every guest is worth honoring, because I never know who is at my door.
try: Welcome one person today, a new colleague or neighbor, more warmly than you normally would.

title: They said peace, and he answered with a fuller peace.
subtitle: Returning a greeting better than it came
then: The guests said salaman; Ibrahim replied salamun. Ibn Kathir explains his reply is {reward}the stronger greeting{/reward}, acting on 4:86: greet back with better or equal. He said: {idea}you are a people unknown to me,{/idea} and still welcomed them.
now: Someone says hi in the corridor and you grunt back without looking up from your phone. {reward}Ibrahim answered strangers with more warmth than they gave.{/reward} {idea}A greeting is the smallest act of hospitality.{/idea}
old: A quick nod is enough when someone greets me.
new: When greeted, I can give back more warmth than I received, even to strangers.
try: Return every greeting today with something fuller: a smile, a name, a full salam.

title: He slipped away to his family and brought a fattened calf.
subtitle: Quiet, quick, generous hospitality
then: Ibn Kathir notes Ibrahim {idea}went inside discreetly and in haste{/idea}, and brought a calf roasted on hot coals, {reward}the best of what he had.{/reward} He did not first say, we will make you food. He simply had it prepared.
now: Friends drop by unannounced. You could say, we were not expecting anyone. Or you could quietly put the kettle on and bring out the good biscuits, the ones saved for Eid. {reward}That is the Ibrahim way.{/reward}
old: Hospitality means offering what is easy and convenient.
new: Real hospitality is quick, quiet, and offers the best I have without announcing it.
try: The next time someone visits, serve them the best thing in your kitchen without asking first.

title: He set it close to them: will you not eat?
subtitle: The gentle way to offer
then: Ibn Kathir draws manners from this: Ibrahim {idea}placed the food close to them{/idea} and did not order them to eat. He invited with a soft question, {reward}will you not eat?{/reward} He compares it to saying, would you be kind enough to?
now: At a family dinner, someone shy sits at the far end and the dishes never reach them. Pass the plate, set it right in front of them, and say, won't you try this? {idea}Small courtesies make guests feel wanted.{/idea}
old: Putting food on the table is enough; people can help themselves.
new: Bringing it close and inviting gently is part of honoring a guest.
try: At your next meal with others, serve someone else first and invite them gently.

title: He felt afraid; they said do not fear, and brought good news.
subtitle: Unease turning into glad tidings
then: Ibn Kathir explains from 11:70: {trap}when he saw their hands did not reach for the food, he felt fear.{/trap} They said do not fear, and {reward}gave him glad tidings of a knowledgeable son,{/reward} Ishaq, news as good for him as for his wife.
now: Your phone buzzes with a missed call from the doctor's surgery and your mind races. Sometimes the call is bad news. Sometimes it is the opposite. {idea}Unease is not a prophecy.{/idea} {reward}Ibrahim's fear was the doorway to his best news.{/reward}
old: When something feels off, I assume the worst.
new: A moment of unease can be the doorway to good news from Allah.
try: The next time you feel sudden dread today, say: O Allah, I ask You for the good in this.

title: His wife cried out: a barren old woman?
subtitle: When good news sounds impossible
then: Ibn Abbas and others said she {idea}came forward crying out{/idea} and struck her forehead, as people do when confronted with something astonishing. She said, Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}how can I give birth, old as I am, when even young I could not have children?{/trap}
now: You have been trying for years, for a child, a cure, a reconciliation, and someone says it could still happen. You almost laugh, it sounds so far away. {idea}Her reaction is honest and human.{/idea} The answer to it comes next.
old: Some doors have been closed too long to ever open.
new: Being astonished by good news is human, but what seems impossible to me is not to Allah.
try: Make dua today for the one thing you stopped asking for because it seemed impossible.

title: Thus has your Lord said; He is the Wise, the Knowing.
subtitle: His word settles what seemed impossible

row.title: Wise, Knowing
sub: knows what you are worthy of

then: The angels answered her: {idea}thus has your Lord said.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains He is {reward}All-Knowing of the honor you are worthy of{/reward} and most Wise in His words and decisions. The family that could not have a child would have Ishaq, and Ya'qub after him.
now: The fertility clinic gave you percentages. The specialist gave you odds. {idea}Those numbers are real, and so is the One above them.{/idea} {reward}When He decides, His wisdom decides the timing too.{/reward}
old: The odds tell me what will and will not happen.
new: My Lord's word and wisdom are above every odd, and He knows what I am worthy of.
try: Write down one hope you have, and under it write: thus has your Lord said; He is the Wise, the Knowing.

title: Ibrahim asked his guests why they had really come.
subtitle: A good host asks the real question

key.label: What he did with the moment

row.title: take the good news and rest

then: The angels had just given Ibrahim the news of a son. His fear was gone. Instead of only enjoying the moment, {idea}he asked what their real mission was.{/idea} The tafsir links this to how he then pleaded for the people of Lut.
now: You get the promotion, the good test result, the yes you wanted. The easy thing is to close the door and celebrate. {idea}Ibrahim's question was about other people.{/idea} Who else is going through something right now?
old: When good news comes, my day is done.
new: Good news for me can open my eyes to what others are facing.
try: After your next bit of good news, message one person who is struggling and ask how they are.

title: The same visitors carried joy for one, warning for another.
subtitle: The mission to the people of Lut
then: The angels answered Ibrahim plainly. They were sent to {trap}a people who were criminals{/trap}, the people of Lut. The same guests who brought Ibrahim glad news carried a very different message to the next town.
now: Two coworkers get called into the same office on the same morning. One leaves smiling, one leaves shaken. {idea}The meeting did not decide that. What came before it did.{/idea}
old: What happens to people is mostly random.
new: Often what reaches us carries the shape of what we did before it came.
try: Think of one habit you would not want to be called in about. Start changing it today, quietly.

title: Stones of clay, sent with purpose.
subtitle: The form the punishment would take
then: The angels named exactly what they carried: {trap}stones of baked clay{/trap} for a people who would not stop. The tafsir calls them stones of sijjil. It was not chance. It was sent.
now: You read about a collapse, a scandal, a ruin, and call it bad luck. Some endings are, but some are the slow result of years of warnings ignored. {idea}The verse asks you to read your own warnings while they are still warnings.{/idea}
old: Consequences just happen to people.
new: Some consequences are answers, and warnings come long before them.
try: Name one warning you have been getting lately, from your body, your family, or your conscience. Write it down.

title: Each stone was marked with its owner's name.
subtitle: Nothing aimed at random
then: The stones were {idea}marked in the presence of your Lord{/idea}. The tafsir says they were recorded with Allah to their names: {trap}each stone has the name of its companion.{/trap} The ones who went too far were known one by one.
now: You tell yourself you are one of millions, one comment in a thread, one face at the party. No one will notice what you did. {idea}You are not a number to Allah.{/idea} Your name is known, and so is every small good you do.
old: In a crowd, what I do disappears.
new: Allah knows me by name, so nothing I do is anonymous.
try: Do one good thing today that no one will see or thank you for.

title: Before the stones fell, the believers were brought out.
subtitle: Rescue came first

row.title: the good die with the bad

then: Ibrahim had worried: Lut is in that town. The tafsir quotes the angels' reply, {idea}we know better who is there.{/idea} So the believers, Lut and his family except his wife, {reward}were brought out first.{/reward}
now: You worry about your children in a hard school, your friend in a toxic workplace, yourself in a city that pulls you the wrong way. {idea}Allah sees who is who inside the crowd.{/idea} Keep your faith, and trust that you are not lost in it.
old: If I live around wrong, I will be swept away with it.
new: Allah knows exactly who holds on, even in the middle of a bad place.
try: Make one dua today for someone you love who lives somewhere hard.

title: In a whole town, only one household held on.
subtitle: Being the one house
then: When the town was searched, {reward}only one household of Muslims{/reward} was found: Lut's family. Even inside it, his wife stayed behind, as the tafsir notes. {trap}The rest of the town had turned away.{/trap}
now: The office where everyone pads expenses. The friend group where everyone mocks the same person. The family where no one prays. {idea}You can be the one house.{/idea} It feels lonely, and it is seen.
old: If everyone around me does it, it cannot be that bad.
new: Allah looks at each house, not at the average of the street.
try: Pick one small thing you do differently from your circle for Allah's sake, and keep doing it today.

title: The ruins were left as a sign for those who fear.
subtitle: Who actually learns from a ruin

key.label: Two ways to pass a ruin

row.title: a mirror
sub: what does this say to me

then: Allah left {trap}a proof of the punishment{/trap} in that place. The tafsir says their dwellings became a putrid, dead sea. {idea}It is a lesson for the believers{/idea}, but only those who fear will read it.
now: You scroll past a story of a family torn apart by one secret, a career ended by one habit. Most people say how sad and keep scrolling. {idea}The person who fears asks: is any of that in me?{/idea}
old: Other people's downfalls are just stories.
new: A ruin is a message, but only to the one who is willing to be warned.
try: Next time you hear of someone's downfall, ask one honest question about yourself before you comment.

title: Musa came to Pharaoh with proof that was plain.
subtitle: The next sign: clear authority
then: After Lut's town, the surah turns to Musa. He was sent to Pharaoh {idea}with a manifest authority{/idea}, which the tafsir explains as clear proof and plain evidence. The problem would never be the proof.
now: You say you would change if you were sure. Then the doctor shows you the scan, the bank shows you the numbers, a friend shows you the pattern. {trap}Still you wait.{/trap} Sometimes the proof is already on the table.
old: I will change once I am completely convinced.
new: Clear proof often arrives early. What is missing is the will to accept it.
try: Name one thing you already know is true but keep asking for more proof about. Act on it in one small way.

title: Pharaoh turned his back and called the messenger names.
subtitle: Labels as a way to avoid the message
then: Pharaoh {trap}turned away in rebellion and arrogance{/trap}, leaning on his supporters. He did not answer Musa's proof. He picked a label: a sorcerer or a madman. The tafsir ties this to bending the neck in pride.
now: Someone points out something true about you and you reply, she is just jealous, he is so dramatic. {trap}The label ends the conversation.{/trap} {idea}It does not end the truth.{/idea}
old: If I can label the critic, I can ignore the criticism.
new: Attacking the messenger is a way of running from the message.
try: Recall one criticism you dismissed by labeling the person. Look at the criticism alone for a minute.

title: The army that backed him sank with him.
subtitle: What his supporters were worth
then: Pharaoh had turned away {reward}with his supporters{/reward}. Now Allah took him and his armies and threw them into the sea. The tafsir says he was {trap}a denying sinner worthy of blame.{/trap}
now: You feel safe because your people are with you: the team, the followers, the family that always takes your side. {idea}Backing is not the same as being right.{/idea} The people who agree with you cannot carry your blame for you.
old: With enough people on my side, I am safe.
new: Support from people does not protect me from being wrong.
try: Ask one person who usually disagrees with you for their honest view on something you are doing.

title: A wind that brought nothing, sent against Aad.
subtitle: The barren wind

row.title: rain carrier
sub: the winds at the surah's start

row.title: barren
sub: the same air, turned against them

then: The surah opened by swearing by winds that scatter and carry rain. Here is the other kind: {trap}the barren wind{/trap} sent against Aad. The tafsir says it destroys everything and {trap}produces nothing{/trap}.
now: The same phone that connects you to family can empty your evenings. The same money that feeds your house can fill it with arguments. {idea}What blesses or harms is in Allah's hand.{/idea} The thing itself is not your safety.
old: The things that serve me will always serve me.
new: The same gift can become a trial. My safety is with Allah, not with things.
try: Pick one thing you rely on daily and say a short thanks to Allah for it before using it.

title: Whatever the wind touched turned to dust.
subtitle: How complete the end was
then: The wind {trap}spared nothing that it reached{/trap}. The tafsir says it made everything like something rotten and destroyed. Aad had been known for their strength and their buildings. None of it held.
now: You spend years on the house, the follower count, the business name. A fire, a market crash, one bad night can flatten it. {idea}What is done for Allah does not crumble that way.{/idea}
old: If I build it strong enough, it will last.
new: Everything I build can fall. What I do for Allah is what remains.
try: Give a little of your time or money today to something that will outlast you.

title: Thamud were told: enjoy yourselves, but only for a while.
subtitle: A deadline given as a warning
then: Thamud were {trap}guided but preferred blindness{/trap}, as the tafsir quotes from another surah. Then they were told to enjoy themselves for a while. The tafsir says they were given three days before the torment came.
now: The free trial ends Friday. The warning letter says thirty days. You treat the gap as more time to relax. {idea}Every respite is a chance to turn around{/idea}, and your life itself is one.
old: Extra time means I can keep going as I am.
new: Extra time is a gift to change, not a pause before nothing.
try: Think of one thing you keep putting off making right. Do the first step before tomorrow.

title: They defied the command, and it hit them while watching.
subtitle: Seeing it coming is not escaping it
then: Thamud {trap}insolently defied the command of their Lord{/trap}. The tafsir says that on the early morning of the fourth day, the blast seized them. {trap}They were looking right at it.{/trap}
now: You watch your health slip, your marriage cool, your prayers thin out. You notice every sign. {idea}Noticing is not the same as turning.{/idea} Knowing a problem is coming does not stop it.
old: As long as I am aware of a problem, I have it under control.
new: Awareness without turning back changes nothing.
try: Take one problem you have been just watching and do one real thing about it today.

title: They could not stand, and no one could help.
subtitle: When all strength runs out
then: When the blast came, Thamud {trap}were unable to rise up{/trap}. The tafsir says they could not run from it, {trap}nor save themselves{/trap}. The strength they were proud of was gone in one moment.
now: Lying in a hospital bed, you learn how little you control. You cannot stand up alone, and the people you counted on can only wait in the corridor. {idea}The time to lean on Allah is now, while you can still stand.{/idea}
old: I can always rely on myself when things get bad.
new: My strength can vanish in a moment. Allah is the help that remains.
try: Stand up from where you are, and say one honest dua asking Allah for help with something you carry.

title: Before all of them, the people of Nuh went the same way.
subtitle: The oldest sign in the list
then: The list of signs ends by going back to the first: {trap}the people of Nuh, before them all.{/trap} The tafsir says Allah destroyed them before Pharaoh, Aad and Thamud. They were a people who {trap}rebelled against what they were told.{/trap}
now: You keep making the same mistake in different jobs, different friendships, different cities. You think each one is a new story. {idea}Look at the pattern, not the scenery.{/idea}
old: Every situation I end up in is different.
new: When the same ending repeats, the cause is usually the same choice.
try: Write down one pattern that keeps repeating in your life. Name the choice behind it.

title: The sky was built with strength and is still being widened.
subtitle: Look up from the ruins
then: After the ruined nations, the surah looks up. The tafsir says Allah made the sky {idea}a high roof, protected from falling{/idea}, built with strength, and {reward}made it vast without pillars to support it.{/reward} It is a proof of His Oneness.
now: You walk to the car with your eyes on your phone. Above you is a roof with no pillars that has not fallen once in your life. {idea}Look up for ten seconds.{/idea} The One who holds that up can hold your day.
old: The sky is just there.
new: The sky is a daily proof that Allah holds what I cannot.
try: Step outside tonight, look up for one full minute, and say SubhanAllah.

title: The earth was spread out like a bed for you.
subtitle: The ground as a gift
then: The tafsir explains that Allah {reward}made the earth a resting place for the created{/reward} and spread it for its inhabitants. He praises Himself: {idea}how excellent a spreader!{/idea} The sky above, the ground below, both point to one Maker.
now: You pay rent or a mortgage and feel you earned the ground you stand on. But the floor under the floor, the soil, water and air, was ready before you were born. {reward}You walked into a prepared room.{/reward}
old: I worked for every bit of ground I have.
new: The ground itself was prepared for me before I did anything.
try: Before sleeping tonight, thank Allah by name for one thing about the place you live.

title: Everything comes in pairs, so you remember the One.
subtitle: Pairs point to the One without a pair

row.title: only the Creator has no pair

then: The tafsir lists the pairs: heaven and earth, night and day, sun and moon, land and sea, {idea}faith and disbelief, misery and happiness, Paradise and Fire.{/idea} All of it so that {reward}you remember the Creator is One.{/reward}
now: Your phone and its charger. Your left hand and your right. Morning coffee and evening tiredness. {idea}Everything you own needs a partner to work.{/idea} The One who made them all needs nothing.
old: Pairs are just how things happen to be.
new: Everything needing another reminds me that Allah alone needs no one.
try: Notice three pairs around you today and, for each, say Allah is One.

title: Run toward Allah, not away from Him.
subtitle: Where to go when you are afraid
then: After the signs in the sky, the earth and the pairs, the call comes: {reward}flee to Allah.{/reward} The tafsir explains it as {idea}seek shelter with Him and trust in Him in all of your affairs.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ is a clear warner from Him.
now: Bad news hits and you run: to the fridge, to scrolling, to blaming, to staying in bed. {idea}The verse points you the other way.{/idea} Run to the One who can actually carry it.
old: When things go wrong, I escape into anything that numbs it.
new: The safest place to run when afraid is toward Allah.
try: Next time you feel the urge to escape, pause and make wudu or say one dua first.

title: Do not put anything beside Allah.
subtitle: The warning repeated, with a new edge
then: The verse before said flee to Allah. This one closes the side door: {trap}do not set up another god with Him.{/trap} The tafsir says do not associate partners with Him. {idea}The same words, I am a clear warner, repeat to drive it home.{/idea}
now: You pray, and also keep a lucky charm, a horoscope app, a quiet belief that your boss really decides your fate. {trap}Small partners creep in.{/trap} {idea}Running to Allah means running to Him alone.{/idea}
old: Trusting Allah and trusting other things too seems harmless.
new: Real shelter in Allah has no partner standing beside Him.
try: Identify one thing you treat as if it controls your fate. Remind yourself today that only Allah does.

title: Every messenger heard the same insult.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ

row.title: I must be doing it wrong

then: The tafsir says {idea}Allah comforts His Prophet ﷺ{/idea} here. The people of Makkah were calling him names. Allah tells him: the disbelievers of old {trap}used the same words with their messengers.{/trap} Pharaoh said them to Musa earlier in this very surah.
now: You start praying at work, or stop drinking, or wear what you believe in. Someone calls you extreme, or weird. {idea}You are not the first.{/idea} The insult is old, and so is the path you are on.
old: If people mock me for doing right, I must be doing something wrong.
new: Mockery for doing right is an old road, walked by every messenger.
try: If someone teases you for your faith this week, answer once, kindly, and let it go.

title: They never met, yet they said the same thing.
subtitle: Same hearts, same words
then: Allah asks: {idea}did the people of the past teach these words to the people of the present?{/idea} The answer is no. The tafsir says they are tyrannical people {trap}whose hearts are the same{/trap}, so they say the same.
now: You catch yourself saying exactly what your father said when he was angry, word for word, though you swore you never would. {idea}The words follow the heart.{/idea} Change what is inside and the words change.
old: My words just come out; they do not mean much.
new: What I say repeatedly shows me what my heart has become.
try: Notice one phrase you say often when frustrated. Ask what feeling sits under it.

title: Turn away from them. You are not to blame.
subtitle: Letting go of what is not yours
then: The tafsir says: {idea}O Muhammad ﷺ, turn away from the Quraysh idolators.{/idea} Allah adds, {reward}We blame you not if you turn away from them.{/reward} He had conveyed the message clearly. Their refusal was not his failure.
now: You keep sending the long message, trying again with the relative who will not listen. You lie awake replaying it. {reward}You are not blamed for their no.{/reward} Say it well, then rest.
old: If someone does not change, it is because I failed them.
new: My job is to speak kindly and clearly. Their answer belongs to them.
try: Think of one person you keep trying to fix. Make dua for them and let the next argument go.

title: Keep reminding. Believing hearts benefit.
subtitle: Turning away is not going silent
then: Right after turn away comes {idea}and remind.{/idea} The tafsir explains: {reward}only the believing hearts benefit from being reminded.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ was not to stop teaching, only to stop chasing those set on refusing.
now: You stopped sharing anything about faith because one cousin always mocks it. But your sister reads every word, and your friend quietly started praying. {reward}Remind for them.{/reward}
old: If some people mock reminders, I should stop giving them.
new: Reminders are for hearts ready to hear. Those hearts are worth it.
try: Share one short, kind reminder today with someone you know is open to it.

title: You were made to worship Him. That is the point.
subtitle: The reason behind everything
then: The tafsir says Allah created them {idea}so that they worship Him alone{/idea}, not that He needs them. It quotes a hadith: {reward}busy yourself in worship and I will fill your chest with riches{/reward}, otherwise the chest fills with distraction.
now: You fill the day with tabs, tasks, and errands, and at night feel empty and busy at once. {idea}The verse names what you were made for.{/idea} Even work, kindness, and rest can be worship when done for Him.
old: Worship is one part of life, squeezed in when I have time.
new: Worship is the reason for my life, and it can run through all of it.
try: Pick one ordinary task today and do it with the intention of pleasing Allah.

title: He wants no food or income from you.
subtitle: A master unlike any other
then: Human masters keep servants so the servants can feed and enrich them. Allah says He wants {idea}no provision from them{/idea} and does not ask to be fed. The tafsir says {reward}they are in need of Him in all conditions{/reward}, not the other way.
now: Your boss needs your hours. Your landlord needs your rent. Even friends sometimes need something back. {idea}Allah asks for your worship and gains nothing from it.{/idea} Every bit of it returns to you.
old: Everyone who asks something of me wants to get something.
new: Allah asks of me only what benefits me. He needs nothing.
try: During your next prayer, remind yourself once that this is for your benefit, not His.

title: Allah is the Provider, strong and firm.
subtitle: Who actually puts food on your table
then: Having said He needs nothing, Allah says what He is: {reward}the All-Provider, Owner of power, the Most Strong.{/reward} The tafsir mentions that the Prophet ﷺ taught these words. {idea}He alone is their Creator and Provider.{/idea}
now: Payday is late, the contract ends, a client disappears. Your stomach drops. {idea}The company was only a channel.{/idea} {reward}The Provider is still the Provider.{/reward}
old: My income depends on my employer.
new: My employer is a door. The Provider is Allah, and He is never weak.
try: When you next check your bank balance, say Ya Razzaq once, and thank Him for today.

title: Their share is coming, so do not ask it to hurry.
subtitle: The same portion as those before
then: The deniers mocked: if punishment is real, bring it now. The tafsir says they will {trap}receive their due share{/trap}, like the nations already described, and {idea}let them not ask that it be rushed, for it will surely come.{/idea}
now: You do something wrong and nothing happens, so you dare it again, almost testing whether anything ever will. {idea}The quiet is not a verdict.{/idea} It is time given to turn back.
old: If nothing bad has happened yet, it probably never will.
new: Delay is a mercy to use, not proof that nothing is coming.
try: Take one wrong you have gotten away with and quietly put it right, or ask Allah's forgiveness for it.

title: The promised Day is coming. Be ready for it.
subtitle: How the surah ends

row.title: prepared
sub: what the surah began with: it is true

then: The surah opened with oaths that the promise is true and the Judgment will happen. It closes with {trap}woe to those who disbelieve{/trap} from their promised Day. The tafsir says this is {idea}the Day of Resurrection.{/idea}
now: You plan for the exam, the wedding, retirement, all days you are not even sure you will see. {idea}One Day is certain.{/idea} {reward}A little preparing for it today makes it a day to look forward to.{/reward}
old: The Day of Judgment is far away and abstract.
new: It is the one appointment I am sure to keep, so I can prepare for it now.
try: Do one deed today you would be glad to find on that Day: a prayer on time, a call to a parent, a gift.
